description:
kith-jmap/src/lib.rs lines 85-93: RequestError is a pub tuple struct:

    pub struct RequestError(pub StatusCode, pub JmapError);

Both fields are pub and are axum/http third-party types (StatusCode from the http crate, JmapError from jmap_types). This means:

1. Any change to http::StatusCode (e.g. version bump with API changes) breaks RequestError's public API.
2. jmap_types::JmapError is already a leakage point from KithError (separate finding); it appears here too, in a different crate.
3. Any code that constructs RequestError via the tuple literal RequestError(status, err) is coupled to both third-party types.
4. The convenience constructor request_error(err: JmapError) is provided (line 96-99) but callers can still construct directly via the tuple, bypassing the standard construction path.

Fix: make both tuple fields pub(crate). The only external use of RequestError is as an axum IntoResponse return type, which only requires the impl — not the field values. Callers should use request_error() or error_invocation() to construct error responses.
title: kith-jmap: RequestError exposes StatusCode and JmapError as pub tuple fields
